text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 10:12:30 UTC - api-gateway-us-east-1: 502/504 error rate spike (10x baseline) — alert threshold breached. P95 latency + upstream timeouts. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/xyz/api-gw-errors

Alex (oncall): seeing the same in Zoomer dashboard, spike started ~10:08. Paging SRE oncall. @Joanna can you take? :rotating_light:

Joanna (sre-lead): on it. first quick check — any deploys around 10:00-10:05? Maria, Kevin?

Maria (prod-eng): no user-facing deploys from prod-eng at that window. We did push a config tweak to edge-logging at 09:50 but that was just log-level.

Kevin (edge): I see increased 502s from edge-proxy v3.4.2 upstream to model-pool. Upstream logs show repeated "upstream timed out" from model-backend(10.12.x).

Alex (oncall): copying a recent sample from nginX error log (sanitized):

```
[10/Mar/2025:10:09:12 +0000] "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1" 502 0 "-" "curl/7.68.0" upstream: "10.12.5.8:8080" host: "api.redwood.ai" request_time: 1.23
```

Joanna (sre-lead): that matches: backends are returning timeout 504 -> edge converts to 502 in some paths. Check model-pool pod restarts/ooms? kubectl top?

Kevin (edge): checking k8s: one of the model-backend replicas in us-east-1-scaledpool-3 is stuck in CrashLoopBackOff, high CPU on others. I can paste pod status.

```
kubectl get pods -n prod | grep model-backend
model-backend-3  CrashLoopBackOff  6/6  0  1m
model-backend-4  Running           6/6  4  20m
model-backend-5  Running           6/6  4  20m
```

Maria (prod-eng): looking into model-backend logs — shows repeated KV-cache eviction spikes and "CUDA OOM" around 10:07 on replica 3. Might be a memory regression in the quantized runtime.

Joanna (sre-lead): ok immediate mitigation options: (1) drain the unhealthy replica, (2) scale up model-backend replicas, (3) shift a % of traffic to us-west-1 fallback region, (4) enable 1-second automatic retry on idempotent requests at the gateway for customers who can accept eventual success. Thoughts?

Alex (oncall): I'd prefer traffic shift + scale up. Retrying at gateway risks ordering/duplicate side effects. Also need to evaluate customer impact before enabling retries.

Kevin (edge): I can change routing policy to shift 30% to us-west-1 via runtime routing (policy id: route-fallback-1). Pushing now.

OpsBot: rolling routing change applied: route-fallback-1 -> 30% traffic to us-west-1. change_id: r-20250310-001.

Joanna (sre-lead): scaling model-backend pool by +4 now (autoscaler temporarily overridden).

OpsBot: HPA override applied: model-backend replicas target increased to 12, rollout initiated.

Kevin (edge): also enabled short-circuit cache for common prompt prefixes on edge for 60s to blunt load.

Maria (prod-eng): confirming pod 3 logs — CUDA OOM due to new quantization micro-optimizations in runtime. Rolling back runtime to previous checksum recommended for immediate stability. Preparing rollout undo for model-runtime.

Alex (oncall): go ahead with rollback. Document the rollout id and start time.

Maria (prod-eng): rollback in progress: kubectl rollout undo deploy/model-runtime -n prod --to-revision=42.

OpsBot: rollback start logged: deploy/model-runtime -> rev 42. expected 2-3min to stabilize.

Joanna (sre-lead): monitoring error rate. P95 dropped from 1.8s to 0.9s after traffic shift and scaling. 502 rate reduced ~60% in ten minutes. Good signal.

Kevin (edge): still seeing tail of errors from long-lived keepalive connections - clearing connections on edge-proxies to force new ones. Command: `edgectl conn reset --region us-east-1 --service api-gw`

Alex (oncall): doing customer impact quick estimate: overall platform error % peaked at 8% in us-east-1, global error rate peaked at 2.3%. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (most), some streaming sessions dropped. Active paying customers affected ~14 (higher-touch) but most saw transient failures.

Ryan (pm): need a short notice for CS and status page. Drafting post now: "We experienced elevated 5xx errors in US-East causing intermittent failures to API requests between 10:08–10:25 UTC. Traffic routed to fallback and service restored. We are investigating root cause (runtime memory regression) and will follow up with a postmortem." Anyone object?

Joanna (sre-lead): fine. Please mark affected customers and include mitigation steps.

Kevin (edge): edge proxies stabilized after conn reset. Datapoints: 502s from 180/min -> 20/min in 15m.

Maria (prod-eng): rollback completed at 10:20. All model-backend replicas reporting Running and healthy by 10:23. No more OOMs in logs.

Joanna (sre-lead): marking incident as mitigated at 10:25 UTC. We'll keep monitoring for 2 hours. Assigning follow-ups: Maria to root-cause (quantization regression), Kevin to edge-proxy connection handling review, Alex to customer-impact list and postmortem draft, Ryan to status updates and CC for affected accounts.

Alex (oncall): handoff note for next shift: mitigated but still under 2-hr watch. Primary actions taken: traffic shift to us-west, scale-up model-backend, rollback runtime, edge conn reset, enable short cache. Follow-ups created in jira: RW-INC-3245.

Joanna (sre-lead): thanks team. If error rate creeps up again we will escalate to SEV1 and trigger pagers. For now, thumbs up :thumbsup: and make sure incident timeline is captured for postmortem.

OpsBot: incident timeline saved to /incidents/1745607890/timeline.log.

Ryan (pm): sending status page now.

Alex (oncall): handing off to Joanna for 10:30–12:30 watch. JoannA, take over monitoring and action items.

Joanna (sre-lead): taking handoff. Logged handoff message in incident doc. Signing off thread but staying watchful.

incident-bot: Incident state changed: MITIGATED -> MONITORING.
